questions.q: What are the four non-negotiable pillars of autonomous database architecture in the chapter?
options: Speed, scale, security, savings
Collect, correlate, classify, decide
Continuous Observability, Closed-Loop Control, Bounded Autonomy, Graceful Degradation
Hub, spoke, sidecar, consensus
questions.explain: The chapter grounds the architecture in Continuous Observability, Closed-Loop Control (OODA loop completing in software), Bounded Autonomy (policy envelopes), and Graceful Degradation (fail toward safety).

questions.q: What observability retention policy does the chapter prescribe?
options: Keep everything at full resolution forever
Short-term high-resolution data (15-second scrape, 15-day retention) for the real-time decision engine; downsampled long-term data (1-minute resolution, 1-year retention) for forecasting models
One year of 15-second data, then delete
Only alerts are retained; raw metrics are discarded
questions.explain: The chapter specifies 15-second scrape with 15-day retention for real-time decisions and 1-minute downsampled data with 1-year retention for forecasting.

questions.q: In the Kubernetes operator reconciliation loop, how is min_confidence_threshold set?
options: 0.95 or higher for destructive or irreversible actions (dropping an index, failover, terminating transactions); 0.75 is sufficient for conservative tuning actions (MAXDOP, query hints)
A fixed 0.50 for every action
1.00 always — no autonomous action may execute below perfect confidence
Randomly per reconciliation cycle
questions.explain: The chapter sets min_confidence_threshold at 0.95+ for destructive/irreversible actions and 0.75 for conservative tuning actions.

questions.q: In the chapter's normalized-signal state machine, a metric with |z-score| above 4 is classified as:
options: NOMINAL
DEGRADED
RECOVERING
CRITICAL
questions.explain: The signal query classifies |z| > 4 as CRITICAL, |z| > 2.5 as DEGRADED, and the rest as NOMINAL (computed against a 30-day baseline).

questions.q: When is the Distributed Consensus topology pattern (Raft via etcd) the right choice for the autonomous control plane?
options: Always — it is the default for every deployment

When the hub-and-spoke control plane introduces unacceptable single-point-of-failure risk, accepting 200–800 ms of decision latency in exchange for quorum-agreed actions that avoid split-brain autonomous actions
Only for development clusters
When you want the lowest possible decision latency
questions.explain: The chapter says consensus is appropriate when hub-and-spoke's single point of failure is unacceptable; it adds 200–800 ms latency but requires quorum before dispatching actions.
